chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from al-Amriki from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)

Regarding the saddle and the bridle, if they contain silver, is it permissible to ride with them? He said: 'If it is embedded such that it cannot be removed, there is no harm; otherwise, do not ride with them.'

key_terms.مُمَوَّهاً: Embedded/Inlaid (where the material is set in such a way that it cannot be easily removed)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to ride a horse with a silver-embedded saddle in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This ruling from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* addresses the permissibility of riding with silver-adorned tack, distinguishing between fixed (mumawwah) and removable silver. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that if the precious metal is integral and cannot be easily detached, it does not constitute the prohibited 'adornment' (takhalluq) associated with luxury, whereas removable silver is discouraged to avoid the appearance of ostentation.
